Prealgebra · Lesson 8.1

Squares and Their Roots

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Squaring a side gives the area, so 52=2552=25. This lesson flips the question. Given that a panel uses exactly 36 tiles in a square, how long was one edge? Recovering the side from the area is the square root.

Problem
A square concrete pad covers 196196 square feet. Find the length of one edge in feet.
Show a hint
  • Squaring a side gives the area, so to get the side back you undo the square. You are hunting for the number that, times itself, lands exactly on 196196.
  • The two landmarks 13×13=16913×13=169 and 15×15=22515×15=225 trap the answer between 1313 and 1515. Only one whole number lives in that gap, so test it by multiplying it by itself.
Show the full solution
132=169132=169 falls short and 152=225152=225 overshoots, so the side is the one whole number in between. Check it, 14×14=19614×14=196, so one edge is 1414​ feet. Squaring a side gives the area, so rooting the area gives the side back.
Problem
A video wall is built from 625625 identical square panels in a perfect square. Since 202=400202=400 and 302=900302=900, the side length is in the twenties. What is 625625​?
Show a hint
  • The side length is a number in the twenties whose square is 625625. Try squaring a value right in the middle of that range and see how close you land.
  • Test 2525. Compute 25×2525×25. If it equals 625625 exactly, then 2525 is the side length, since the square root recovers the side of a square from its area.
Show the full solution
The side is in the twenties, so try the middle of that range. 25×25=62525×25=625 exactly, so 625=25625​=25​ panels along one side. Squaring two landmarks first pins a root into a small range, which leaves only a guess or two to test.
Key idea
Square root. The square root of nn, written nn​, is the nonnegative number whose square is nn, so 196=14196​=14 because 142=196142=196. Squaring and taking a square root undo each other. A perfect square is a whole number made by multiplying some whole number by itself, like 81=9281=92 or 144=122144=122. The root of a perfect square is always a whole number. Once you know the squares of 11 through about 2020, you can read most roots straight off.

The radical 3636​ names a single value, 66, the nonnegative side of a square with area 3636. The equation x2=36x2=36 asks something different. It wants every number whose square is 3636, and there are two of those, 66 and −6−6. The two questions look alike on the page, so read carefully to tell which one a problem is handing you.

Problem
Both 1010 and −10−10 square to 100100, so two numbers satisfy x2=100x2=100. But the radical 100100​ names only one of them, the nonnegative one. Evaluate 100100​.
Show a hint
  • The radical does not mean "any number that squares to 100". It means the one nonnegative number whose square is 100. Of the two candidates 10 and −10−10, only one is zero or positive.
  • Ask which value is nonnegative. Since 102=100102=100 and 10 is positive, the radical names 10, not −10−10.
Show the full solution
102=100102=100 and 1010 is nonnegative, so 100=10100​=10​. Both 1010 and −10−10 square to 100100, but the radical is defined to name only the nonnegative one, so it never reports −10−10.
Problem
The equation x2=49x2=49 asks for every number whose square is 4949. Since 72=4972=49 and (−7)2=49(−7)2=49, both 77 and −7−7 work. How many values of xx satisfy x2=49x2=49?
Show a hint
  • Squaring a negative number gives a positive result, so do not stop at the first number you find. Try both a positive and a negative candidate and square each one.
  • Check 7272 and check (−7)2(−7)2. If both land on 4949, then count how many separate values of xx you have found.
Show the full solution
72=4972=49, and since a negative times a negative is positive, (−7)2=49(−7)2=49 as well. Nothing else squares to 4949, so exactly 22​ values work, 77 and −7−7. The equation keeps both, while 4949​ reports only the nonnegative 77.
Problem
A depth sensor satisfies x2=324x2=324. Two values work: x=18x=18 and x=−18x=−18. Since depth is negative, which value is xx?
Show a hint
  • Find the two numbers whose square is 324324. Take the square root of 324324 to get the size, then remember the negative version squares to 324324 as well.
  • The size of xx is 324=18324​=18, so xx is 1818 or −18−18. Since xx measures a depth below the surface, it must be negative, which rules out 1818.
Show the full solution
Since 182=324182=324, the two numbers that square to 324324 are 1818 and −18−18. A depth below the surface is negative, so x=−18x=−18​. Squaring erases the sign, so the equation alone leaves both candidates and the story decides which one you keep.
Problem
Squaring any real number gives a result that is zero or positive. So how many real values of xx satisfy x2=−9x2=−9?
Show a hint
  • Try a few numbers. 32=932=9, (−3)2=9(−3)2=9, 02=002=0. Every square you get is 00 or positive. Can any of them ever equal −9−9?
  • Since squaring any real number gives a result of 00 or more, no real number can square to a negative like −9−9. Count how many real xx work, and that count is the answer.
Show the full solution
A positive squared is positive, a negative squared is positive, and 02=002=0. That covers every real number, so a square is always 00 or greater and nothing can reach −9−9. The count of real solutions is 00​.
Key idea
The radical names one value. An equation can have two. Both 1010 and −10−10 square to 100100, but the radical 100100​ names only the nonnegative one, called the principal root. So 100=10100​=10 and never −10−10. Solving x2=nx2=n is a different question. For positive nn it has two answers, a positive value and its negative, so x2=36x2=36 gives 66 and −6−6 while 3636​ gives just 66. Extra context, like knowing xx is a depth, tells you which one to keep. Squaring any real number gives zero or a positive result, so a negative like −9−9 has no real square root, and x2=−9x2=−9 has no real solution.
Problem
Evaluate (−12)2(−12)2​. Square first, then take the root. What whole number do you get?
Show a hint
  • Follow the order of operations and square first. What is (−12)2(−12)2? Remember that a negative times a negative gives a positive result, so the inside becomes a positive number before you ever touch the radical.
  • Once the inside is 144144, you just need 144144​. Find the nonnegative number whose square is 144144. The radical always reports the nonnegative root, so the sign you started with does not survive.
Show the full solution
Square first. (−12)2=144(−12)2=144, and 144=12144​=12, so the value is 1212​. Squaring drops the sign and the radical returns the nonnegative root, which is why the answer comes out positive even though the number inside started negative.
Problem
A square garden covers 1,2961,296 sq ft. Notice 1,296=16×811,296=16×81. Use 1,296=16×811,296​=16​×81​ to find the side length.
Show a hint
  • Split the work using 1,296=16×811,296=16×81. You can take the root of each piece on its own, since 16×81=16×8116×81​=16​×81​.
  • Find each small root, then multiply them. 16=416​=4 because 42=1642=16, and 81=981​=9 because 92=8192=81. Now compute 4×94×9.
Show the full solution
Since 1,296=16×811,296=16×81, the root splits, so 1,296=16×81=4×9=361,296​=16​×81​=4×9=36. Checking, 36×36=1,29636×36=1,296, so the side is 3636​ feet. Splitting into perfect-square factors turns one hard root into two easy ones.
Problem
A classmate claims 1024=341024​=34. But 342=1156>1024342=1156>1024, and a number ending in 4 squares to something ending in 6, not 4. What is the correct value of 10241024​?
Show a hint
  • The size test says the root sits below 34, and the last-digit test says it cannot end in 4. So try a slightly smaller whole number and square it to see if you hit 1,0241,024 on the nose.
  • You want a number whose square ends in 4. A number ending in 2 works, since 2×2=42×2=4. Check 322322.
Show the full solution
The root sits below 3434, and it has to end in 22, since only a number ending in 22 squares to something ending in 44. That points at 3232, and 32×32=1,02432×32=1,024 exactly, so 1024=321024​=32​. The size check and the last-digit check together usually leave a single candidate to test.
Key idea
Two rules for roots. Squaring and taking a square root undo each other, giving (n)2=n(n​)2=n and n2=nn2​=n for nonnegative nn. Watch the sign, though, since a root only returns a nonnegative value. Squaring −12−12 gives a positive result, so (−12)2=12(−12)2​=12, not −12−12. The product rule ab=a×bab​=a​×b​ lets you root a big perfect square in pieces, so 1,296=16×81=4×9=361,296​=16​×81​=4×9=36. Split it only where each piece is itself a perfect square, so every root stays a whole number.
Fun fact
The word radical comes from Latin radix (root), the same as the vegetable radish. Rudolff used nn​ in 1525. The bar on top, the vinculum, marks what sits under the root.
Problem
A square herb bed has a side of 1515 feet, so x=15x​=15 where xx is the area. Square both sides to free xx. What is xx?
Show a hint
  • The variable is stuck under the radical sign. Whatever you do to one side of an equation you must do to the other, so apply the same operation to both sides that will cancel the square root.
  • Squaring undoes a square root. The left side (x)2(x​)2 collapses back to just xx, and the right side becomes 152152. Now just compute 152152.
Show the full solution
Square both sides. (x)2=152(x​)2=152 The left side collapses to xx, and 152=225152=225, so x=225x=225​ square feet. Squaring is the move that frees a variable from under a radical, and the check holds, since 225=15225​=15.
Key idea
Solving x=kx​=k. When the unknown is under a radical, square both sides to remove it, so (x)2=k2(x​)2=k2 gives x=k2x=k2. The same step clears a whole expression under the root, so 3x+4=113x+4​=11 becomes 3x+4=1213x+4=121, an ordinary linear equation. It works only when k≥0k≥0, because a radical never equals a negative number. So x−2=−4x−2​=−4 has no solution, even though squaring both sides gives an answer.
Problem
Solve 3x+4=113x+4​=11. Square both sides, then solve the resulting linear equation. What is xx?
Show a hint
  • Squaring is the move that undoes a square root. If 3x+4=113x+4​=11, then squaring both sides gives 3x+4=1123x+4=112. Work out 112112 first.
  • Now 3x+4=1213x+4=121 is just a linear equation like the ones from Chapter 6. Subtract 44 from both sides, then divide by 33.
Show the full solution
Squaring both sides gives 3x+4=112=1213x+4=112=121. Subtract 44 to get 3x=1173x=117, then divide by 33, so x=39x=39​. Checking, 3×39+4=1213×39+4=121 and 121=11121​=11. Squaring clears the radical and leaves an ordinary linear equation.
Problem
How many solutions does x−2=−4x−2​=−4 have?
Show a hint
  • The radical xx​ always means the nonnegative root. So whatever x−2x−2 turns out to be, can x−2x−2​ ever come out negative?
  • Try the tempting answer anyway. Squaring gives x=18x=18, and then 18−2=16=418−2​=16​=4, not −4−4. So even that candidate fails the check. If the one value squaring hands you does not work, count how many values are left.
Show the full solution
The radical always returns a value that is zero or positive, and the right side is −4−4, so nothing can match. Squaring hands you x−2=16x−2=16 and x=18x=18, but 18−2=16=418−2​=16​=4, not −4−4, so that candidate fails too. The number of solutions is 00​. Squaring can produce answers that do not satisfy the original equation, which is why you check every candidate back.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A square garden bed covers 121121 sq ft. What is the side length, in feet? Evaluate 121121​.
Show the solution
102=100102=100 is too small and 122=144122=144 is too big, so try 1111. Since 11×11=12111×11=121, the bed is 1111​ feet on a side.
Practice
A square rug covers 256256 sq ft. What is its side length in feet?
Show the solution
The side length is 256256​. Since 152=225152=225 is too small and 172=289172=289 is too big, test 1616, and 16×16=25616×16=256. The rug is 1616​ feet on a side.
Practice
A square patio covers 169169 sq ft. Since 102=100102=100 and 202=400202=400, the side length is between 1010 and 2020. Find 169169​.
Show the solution
The root is between 1010 and 2020, and since 169169 ends in 99 the root must end in 33 or 77. Testing the smaller option, 13×13=16913×13=169, so each side of the patio is 1313​ feet.
Practice
When you write x2=9x2=9, both 33 and −3−3 work. But 99​ names only the nonnegative one. Evaluate 99​.
Show the solution
3×3=93×3=9 and 33 is nonnegative, so 9=39​=3​. The equation x2=9x2=9 keeps both 33 and −3−3, but the radical names only the nonnegative one.
Practice
A square garden covers 400400 sq ft. What is 400400​?
Show the solution
Split into perfect-square factors, since 400=4×100400=4×100. Then 400=4×100=2×10=20400​=4​×100​=2×10=20, and squaring back gives 202=400202=400. The garden is 2020​ feet on a side.
Practice
Both 99 and −9−9 square to 8181, since 92=8192=81 and (−9)2=81(−9)2=81. How many values of xx satisfy x2=81x2=81?
Show the solution
92=8192=81, and a negative times a negative is positive, so (−9)2=81(−9)2=81 as well. Nothing else squares to 8181, so exactly 22​ values work, 99 and −9−9. Solving x2=81x2=81 gives a pair, while evaluating 8181​ gives just 99.
Practice
The equation x2=225x2=225 has two solutions, 1515 and −15−15. Engineers know xx is negative. What is xx?
Show the solution
Since 152=225152=225, both 1515 and −15−15 satisfy x2=225x2=225. The engineers know xx is negative, so x=−15x=−15​. The equation keeps both roots, and the context tells you which one to report.
Practice
Squaring any real number gives zero or a positive result, never negative. How many real values of xx satisfy x2=−16x2=−16?
Show the solution
A positive squared is positive, a negative squared is positive, and 02=002=0, so x2x2 is never negative for a real xx. Nothing can square to −16−16, so the count of real solutions is 00​.
Practice
Squaring undoes a square root and vice versa. Evaluate (47)2(47​)2 without finding the decimal value of 4747​.
Show the solution
4747​ is the nonnegative number whose square is 4747, so squaring it hands 4747 straight back, giving (47)2=47(47​)2=47​. No decimal is needed, since squaring and the square root undo each other for any nonnegative number.
Practice
A recorded side length of −8−8 has the wrong sign. Evaluate (−8)2(−8)2​ to recover the nonnegative side length.
Show the solution
Square first, (−8)2=64(−8)2=64, then take the root, 64=864​=8​. Squaring drops the sign and the radical returns the nonnegative value, so x2x2​ gives the size rather than the original −8−8.
Practice
A square hall uses 4,9004,900 tiles. Since 4,900=49×1004,900=49×100, use 4,900=49×1004,900​=49​×100​ to find the number of tiles along one edge.
Show the solution
Since 4,900=49×1004,900=49×100, the root splits, so 4,900=49×100=7×10=704,900​=49​×100​=7×10=70. Checking, 702=4,900702=4,900, so one edge of the hall holds 7070​ tiles.
Practice
A friend claims 289=17289​=17. Does 172=289172=289? What is 289289​?
Show the solution
17×17=28917×17=289 exactly, so the friend is right and 289=17289​=17​. The last-digit clue agrees, since a square ending in 99 can only come from a root ending in 33 or 77.
Practice
You know x=19x​=19. Square both sides to find xx. What is xx?
Show the solution
Square both sides. The left side gives back xx, and the right gives 192=361192=361, so x=361x=361​. Checking the original, 361=19361​=19 since 19×19=36119×19=361.
Practice
A game requires solving x+7=−3x+7​=−3. The radical is always nonnegative. How many solutions exist?
Show the solution
The radical is always zero or positive, and −3−3 is negative, so no value of xx can make the two sides match. The count is 00​. Squaring would give x+7=9x+7=9 and x=2x=2, but 2+7=32+7​=3, not −3−3, so even that candidate fails the check.
